raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

- Kimi-K3's MLA applies no RoPE, yet on ROCm every absorbed decode and target-verify step still runs two separate launches before attention: it builds the query (`cat(q_nope, q_pe)`) and writes the latent KV cache (`kv_layers.layer(i).store(...)`).
- At AgentX decode batch sizes, those small launches add per-step latency to each of the 24 MLA layers.
- AITER's `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` does both in one launch. With one-row identity cos/sin tables and all-zero positions its RoPE step is a no-op, so the Q and cache bytes it writes match the split chain exactly.

## Modifications

- `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.mla_q_cache_aiter_hip` (op `attention.kimi_k3_mla_q_cache`): a fail-closed adapter for gfx950. `covered()` checks the contract and `run()` launches the op.
- `srt/models/kimi_k3_rocm_mla.KimiK3RocmMlaQCacheWriter`: installed on K3 MLA layers when the switch is set on ROCm. It uses the AITER HIP op on gfx950 and AITER's no-RoPE Triton kernel elsewhere, logging one warning on fallback.
- Memory: Q and the `k` placeholder are allocated per call and are the same size as the `cat` outputs they replace. The only persistent state is one shared int64 zero-position buffer (8 B per token).
- CUDA is unchanged.

| Env var | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_MLA_Q_CACHE_FUSION` | `false` | Write the K3 MLA decode/verify query and latent KV cache in one launch |

| Condition | Path |
|---|---|
| AITER decode or target-verify, Triton decode; no DCP; KV scale 1 (K3 loads none) | Fused Q + cache write |
| gfx950 with the AITER HIP op, inputs inside its contract (BF16 or e4m3fn cache) | AITER HIP op |
| Otherwise, AITER Triton no-RoPE kernel available | AITER Triton kernel |
| Neither kernel available (old AITER, gfx1250) | Split chain, one warning |
| Triton target-verify (its extend kernel reads `k`) | Split chain |
| Non-unit KV scale (the split AITER write ignores it; the fused kernels divide by it) | Split chain |
| DCP, extend, other attention backends | Split chain |

## Accuracy Tests

- GSM8K: sgl-eval 0.1.3, 1,319 questions, `--load-preset-from-model-id moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking on).
- With DSpark speculative decoding: block 3, AITER decode and target-verify, real acceptance, Kimi-K3 AgentX c4 shape, TP8, K3 integration build.

| | Switch off | Switch on |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 97.35% (1 run) | 97.19%, 97.42%, 97.12% (avg 97.24%) |
| Mean accept length (max 4) | 3.14 | 3.18 |

- Without speculative decoding (earlier head): 97.12% off vs 97.50% on.
- Kernel and writer tests (`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_mla_q_cache_aiter_hip.py`, MI355X): for BF16 and FP8 caches, Q and cache bytes are identical to the split chain, and a captured graph still replays correctly after a larger eager batch replaces the shared buffer.
- Gate tests (`test/registered/unit/models/test_rocm_mla_absorb_fusion_gate.py`, CPU): Triton verify, non-unit KV scale, other backends, DCP/extend, and a missing Triton fallback all keep the split chain.
- At the current head, these two files plus `test_kernels_namespace.py`: 150 passed on MI355X.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Setup: 8x MI355X, TP8, `Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`, K3 integration build. Random 8192 in / 1024 out, radix cache off, 4 x C prompts. Switch off and on alternated, 3 runs per side (spread <= 0.1 ms).

| Conc | TPOT off (ms) | TPOT on (ms) | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 15.66 | 15.26 | -2.6% |
| 16 | 24.02 | 23.58 | -1.8% |
| 64 | 46.30 | 45.98 | -0.7% |

- TTFT does not change (decode-only path).
- Profile: `aiter::fuse_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla_per_head_kernel` launches once per MLA layer (24) per decode step, replacing the `cat` and the KV-cache write.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

<!-- mintlify-fork-preview-approval -->
### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `afa9dc5`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43127/checks?check_run_id=126468363717)

@yuychang The NV base `base-a-test-cpu` shard fails on this PR's own test, `test/registered/unit/models/test_rocm_mla_absorb_fusion_gate.py` ([job log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40808276640/job/123260121488)). Rerunning won't fix it:

```
ERROR: test_fused_routes (TestKimiK3MlaQCacheWriterGate) (backend='aiter', verify=False)
  File ".../kimi_k3_rocm_mla.py", line 120, in write
  File ".../kimi_k3_rocm_mla.py", line 45, in get
  File ".../torch/cuda/graphs.py", line 92, in is_current_stream_capturing
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
```

`_ZeroPositions.get()` calls `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` even when the device is CPU. The test is registered with `register_cpu_ci`, and the CPU runner has no usable CUDA driver, so the call fails there. One possible fix is to check the device type first:

```diff
-            if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            if device.type == "cuda" and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
```

(ROCm tensors also report `device.type == "cuda"`, so the graph-capture guard still applies on MI35x.) I haven't run the CPU test locally with this change, so please double-check that nothing else in the CPU path touches CUDA.

The merged shape is only faster while the projection is bandwidth bound. 256 + + SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_MLA_Q_CACHE_FUSION + Kimi-K3 on ROCm: write the absorbed MLA decode and target-verify query and the latent KV cache in one launch, with AITER on gfx950 and the AITER Triton kernel elsewhere. +        target="sglang.kernels.ops.attention.mla_q_cache_aiter_hip:run",
+        capabilities=frozenset({CapabilityRequirement.HIP}),

 # Public entry points inventoried by logical operator group (RFC #29630).

@@ -0,0 +1,207 @@
+"""Fail-closed adapter for Kimi-K3's fused MLA Q materialization and cache write."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+
+import torch
+
+# Kimi-K3 MLA widths (kv_lora_rank, qk_rope_head_dim); other widths are not covered.
+_KV_LORA_RANK = 512
+_PE_DIM = 64
+_HEAD_DIM = _KV_LORA_RANK + _PE_DIM
+# The op takes only AITER_DTYPE_fp8, which is e4m3fn on gfx950.
+_FP8_DTYPE = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _op():
+    try:
+        import aiter
+
+        return aiter.fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla
+    except (AttributeError, ImportError):
+        return None
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _is_gfx950() -> bool:
+    try:
+        from aiter.jit.utils.chip_info import get_gfx_runtime
+
+        return get_gfx_runtime() == "gfx950"
+    except (AssertionError, ImportError, KeyError, RuntimeError):
+        return False
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def available() -> bool:
+    return (
+        torch.version.hip is not None
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and _is_gfx950()
+        and _op() is not None
+    )
+
+
+def covered(
+    *,
+    q_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    q_pe: torch.Tensor,
+    k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    k_pe: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    k_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    q_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> bool:
+    if not available() or q_nope.device.type != "cuda" or q_nope.ndim != 3:
+        return False
+    tokens, heads, _ = q_nope.shape
+    q_scale = k_scale if q_scale is None else q_scale
+    tensors = (
+        q_pe,
+        k_nope,
+        k_pe,
+        kv_cache,
+        slot_mapping,
+        positions,
+        k_scale,
+        q_scale,
+        cos_cache,
+        sin_cache,
+        out,
+    )
+    return (
+        tokens > 0
+        and q_nope.shape == (tokens, heads, _KV_LORA_RANK)
+        and q_pe.shape == (tokens, heads, _PE_DIM)
+        and k_nope.shape == (tokens, 1, _KV_LORA_RANK)
+        and k_pe.shape == (tokens, 1, _PE_DIM)
+        and all(
+            x.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and x.stride(-1) == 1
+            for x in (q_nope, q_pe, k_nope, k_pe)
+        )
+        and all(x.device == q_nope.device for x in tensors)
+        and kv_cache.ndim in (3, 4)
+        and kv_cache.shape[-1] == _HEAD_DIM
+        and kv_cache.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, _FP8_DTYPE)
+        and slot_mapping.shape == (tokens,)
+        # AITER's gfx950 kernels take one int64 slot and position per token.
+        and slot_mapping.dtype == torch.int64
+        and slot_mapping.stride(0) == 1
+        and positions.shape == (tokens,)
+        and positions.dtype == torch.int64
+        and positions.stride(0) == 1
+        and k_scale.numel() == 1
+        and k_scale.dtype == torch.float32
+        and k_scale.device == q_nope.device
+        and q_scale.numel() == 1
+        and q_scale.dtype == torch.float32
+        and q_scale.device == q_nope.device
+        and cos_cache.shape == (1, _PE_DIM // 2)
+        and sin_cache.shape == (1, _PE_DIM // 2)
+        and cos_cache.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and sin_cache.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and cos_cache.device == q_nope.device
+        and sin_cache.device == q_nope.device
+        and out.ndim == 3
+        and out.shape[0] == tokens
+        # Extra out heads stay untouched,
+        # so 12-head K3 can write a 16-head MLA pad buffer.
+        and out.shape[1] >= heads
+        and out.shape[2] == _HEAD_DIM
+        # AITER decode wants FP8 Q with FP8 KV,
+        # Triton decode wants BF16 Q with FP8 KV.
+        and out.dtype in (q_nope.dtype, kv_cache.dtype)
+        and out.is_contiguous()
+    )
+
+
+def run(
+    *,
+    q_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    q_pe: torch.Tensor,
+    k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    k_pe: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    k_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    q_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Write the latent KV cache and MLA query for the supported gfx950 contract."""
+    if not available():
+        raise RuntimeError("fused MLA Q/cache requires AITER on gfx950")
+    if not covered(
+        q_nope=q_nope,
+        q_pe=q_pe,
+        k_nope=k_nope,
+        k_pe=k_pe,
+        kv_cache=kv_cache,
+        slot_mapping=slot_mapping,
+        positions=positions,
+        k_scale=k_scale,
+        cos_cache=cos_cache,
+        sin_cache=sin_cache,
+        out=out,
+        q_scale=q_scale,
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("unsupported inputs for fused MLA Q/cache")
+    return launch(
+        q_nope=q_nope,
+        q_pe=q_pe,
+        k_nope=k_nope,
+        k_pe=k_pe,
+        kv_cache=kv_cache,
+        slot_mapping=slot_mapping,
+        positions=positions,
+        k_scale=k_scale,
+        cos_cache=cos_cache,
+        sin_cache=sin_cache,
+        out=out,
+        q_scale=q_scale,
+    )
+
+
+def launch(
+    *,
+    q_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    q_pe: torch.Tensor,
+    k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    k_pe: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    k_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    q_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """run() without its checks, for callers that already passed covered()."""
+    _op()(
+        q_nope,
+        q_pe,
+        k_nope,
+        k_pe,
+        kv_cache,
+        out,
+        slot_mapping,
+        k_scale,
+        k_scale if q_scale is None else q_scale,
+        positions,
+        cos_cache,
+        sin_cache,
+        True,  # is_neox
+        True,  # is_nope_first
+        compute_all_q_rope=False,
+    )
+    return out

+    # AITER on gfx950 and AITER Triton elsewhere, instead of the split chain.

@@ -1173,6 +1183,34 @@ def forward_absorb_rocm_core(
         else:
             return output, topk_indices

+"""Kimi-K3 ROCm MLA decode: write the query and the latent KV cache in one launch.
+
+K3 MLA applies no RoPE. The gfx950 HIP op has only a RoPE form, so it runs against
+one-row identity cos/sin tables with all-zero positions; the Triton fallback uses
+AITER's no-RoPE kernel.
+"""
+
+import functools
+from typing import Callable, Optional, Tuple
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention import mla_q_cache_aiter_hip
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_buffer
+from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_device_stream_capturing, print_warning_once
+
+# With save_kv_cache=False, these backends read only the BF16 Q and the KV cache;
+# Triton target-verify runs its extend kernel, which also reads k.
+_DECODE_BACKENDS = frozenset({"aiter", "triton"})
+_TARGET_VERIFY_BACKENDS = frozenset({"aiter"})
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _triton_q_cache_op() -> Optional[Callable]:
+    """AITER's no-RoPE Triton Q/cache kernel, or None where it cannot run."""
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_properties().gcnArchName.startswith("gfx1250"):
+        return None
+    try:
+        from aiter.ops.triton.fusions.fused_kv_cache import fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla
+    except ImportError:
+        return None
+    return fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla
+
+
+class _ZeroPositions:
+    """Int64 zeros that every K3 MLA layer passes as the identity-RoPE positions."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.buf: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+        self.retired: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+
+    def get(self, tokens: int, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+        buf = self.buf
+        if buf is None or buf.numel() < tokens or buf.device != device:
+            if is_device_stream_capturing(device):
+                # A memset recorded into a graph runs only at replay,
+                # so it cannot seed the shared buffer.
+                return torch.zeros((tokens,), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+            if buf is not None:
+                # Captured graphs keep reading the old pointer;
+                # power-of-two growth keeps retired buffers smaller than the live one.
+                self.retired.append(buf)
+            rows = 1 << (tokens - 1).bit_length()
+            self.buf = buf = torch.zeros((rows,), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+        return buf[:tokens]
+
+
+class KimiK3RocmMlaQCacheWriter(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, kv_lora_rank: int, qk_rope_head_dim: int) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self._kv_lora_rank = kv_lora_rank
+        self._qk_rope_head_dim = qk_rope_head_dim
+        self._head_dim = kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim
+        half_rope_dim = qk_rope_head_dim // 2
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "_identity_cos",
+            torch.ones((1, half_rope_dim), dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            persistent=False,
+        )
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "_identity_sin",
+            torch.zeros((1, half_rope_dim), dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            persistent=False,
+        )
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "_unit_scale", torch.ones((1,), dtype=torch.float32), persistent=False
+        )
+
+    def write(
+        self,
+        *,
+        q_nope: torch.Tensor,
+        q_pe: torch.Tensor,
+        k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+        k_pe: torch.Tensor,
+        out_cache_loc: torch.Tensor,
+        kv_cache: torch.Tensor,
+        k_scale_float: Optional[float],
+        attention_backend: str,
+        is_target_verify: bool,
+    ) -> Optional[Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+        """Return (q, k placeholder) after writing Q and the KV cache,
+        or None to leave both to the split rope/concat/cache chain."""
+        backends = _TARGET_VERIFY_BACKENDS if is_target_verify else _DECODE_BACKENDS
+        if (
+            attention_backend not in backends
+            # The split chain's AITER write casts without the scale,
+            # its Triton decode write divides by it; they agree only at 1.
+            or k_scale_float not in (None, 1.0)
+            or not self._shapes_match(
+                q_nope=q_nope,
+                q_pe=q_pe,
+                k_nope=k_nope,
+                k_pe=k_pe,
+                out_cache_loc=out_cache_loc,
+            )
+        ):
+            return None
+
+        tokens, num_heads = q_nope.shape[0], q_nope.shape[1]
+        kernel_args = dict(
+            q_nope=q_nope,
+            q_pe=q_pe,
+            k_nope=k_nope,
+            k_pe=k_pe,
+            kv_cache=kv_cache,
+            # AITER reads slot_mapping with stride 1, as in the split chain.
+            slot_mapping=out_cache_loc.contiguous(),
+            k_scale=self._unit_scale,
+        )
+        q = self._write_aiter(kernel_args=kernel_args, num_heads=num_heads)
+        if q is None:
+            q = self._write_triton(kernel_args=kernel_args)
+        if q is None:
+            return None
+        # The KV cache is already written; attention reads only the shape of k.
+        k_placeholder = torch.empty(
+            (tokens, 1, self._head_dim), dtype=k_nope.dtype, device=k_nope.device
+        )
+        return q, k_placeholder
+
+    def _shapes_match(
+        self,
+        *,
+        q_nope: torch.Tensor,
+        q_pe: torch.Tensor,
+        k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+        k_pe: torch.Tensor,
+        out_cache_loc: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> bool:
+        tokens, num_heads = q_nope.shape[0], q_nope.shape[1]
+        return (
+            tokens > 0
+            and q_nope.shape == (tokens, num_heads, self._kv_lora_rank)
+            and q_pe.shape == (tokens, num_heads, self._qk_rope_head_dim)
+            and k_nope.shape == (tokens, 1, self._kv_lora_rank)
+            and k_pe.shape == (tokens, 1, self._qk_rope_head_dim)
+            and out_cache_loc.shape == (tokens,)
+        )
+
+    def _write_aiter(
+        self, *, kernel_args: dict, num_heads: int
+    ) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+        if not mla_q_cache_aiter_hip.available():
+            print_warning_once(
+                "Kimi-K3 MLA Q/cache fusion: the AITER op needs gfx950 and an "
+                "AITER build with fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla; using the "
+                "AITER Triton kernel instead."
+            )
+            return None
+        q_nope = kernel_args["q_nope"]
+        aiter_args = dict(
+            kernel_args,
+            # The identity tables have one row and not every kernel clamps positions,
+            # so every token reads row 0.
+            positions=get_buffer("kimi_k3_mla_zero_positions", _ZeroPositions).get(
+                tokens=q_nope.shape[0], device=q_nope.device
+            ),
+            cos_cache=self._identity_cos,
+            sin_cache=self._identity_sin,
+            out=torch.empty(
+                (q_nope.shape[0], num_heads, self._head_dim),
+                dtype=q_nope.dtype,
+                device=q_nope.device,
+            ),
+            q_scale=self._unit_scale,
+        )
+        if not mla_q_cache_aiter_hip.covered(**aiter_args):
+            print_warning_once(
+                "Kimi-K3 MLA Q/cache fusion: inputs are outside the AITER op's "
+                "contract (dtype, stride or cache layout); using the AITER "
+                "Triton kernel instead."
+            )
+            return None
+        return mla_q_cache_aiter_hip.launch(**aiter_args)
+
+    def _write_triton(self, *, kernel_args: dict) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+        fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla = _triton_q_cache_op()
+        if fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla is None:
+            print_warning_once(
+                "Kimi-K3 MLA Q/cache fusion: no AITER Triton fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla "
+                "for this device or AITER build; keeping the split chain."
+            )
+            return None
+        q, _, _, _ = fused_qk_cat_and_cache_mla(
+            kernel_args["q_nope"],
+            kernel_args["q_pe"],
+            kernel_args["k_nope"],
+            kernel_args["k_pe"],
+            kernel_args["kv_cache"],
+            kernel_args["slot_mapping"],
+            kernel_args["k_scale"],
+            q_out_dtype=kernel_args["q_nope"].dtype,
+        )
+        return q

+def _inputs(tokens: int, cache_dtype=torch.bfloat16, output_dtype=None):
+    torch.manual_seed(23)
+    heads = 12
+    q_nope = torch.randn(
+        tokens, heads, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    ).contiguous()
+    q_pe = torch.randn(
+        tokens, heads, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    ).contiguous()
+    k_nope = torch.randn(
+        tokens, 1, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    ).contiguous()
+    k_pe = torch.randn(tokens, 1, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).contiguous()
+    return {
+        "q_nope": q_nope,
+        "q_pe": q_pe,
+        "k_nope": k_nope,
+        "k_pe": k_pe,
+        "kv_cache": torch.zeros(tokens + 4, 1, 576, device="cuda", dtype=cache_dtype),
+        "slot_mapping": torch.arange(tokens, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64),
+        # The cos/sin tables have one identity row, so every position must be 0.
+        "positions": torch.zeros(tokens, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64),
+        "k_scale": torch.ones(1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32),
+        "q_scale": torch.ones(1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32),
+        "cos_cache": torch.ones(1, 32, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+        "sin_cache": torch.zeros(1, 32, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+        "out": torch.empty(
+            tokens,
+            heads,
+            576,
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=cache_dtype if output_dtype is None else output_dtype,
+        ),
+    }
+
+
+def _reference(values):
+    return (
+        torch.cat((values["q_nope"], values["q_pe"]), dim=-1).to(values["out"].dtype),
+        torch.cat((values["k_nope"], values["k_pe"]), dim=-1).to(
+            values["kv_cache"].dtype
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 4, 8, 64, 128, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("cache_dtype", "output_dtype"),
+    [
+        (torch.bfloat16, torch.bfloat16),
+        (dtypes.fp8, dtypes.fp8),
+        (dtypes.fp8, torch.bfloat16),
+    ],
+)
+def test_fused_mla_q_cache_identity_rope(tokens, cache_dtype, output_dtype):
+    values = _inputs(tokens, cache_dtype=cache_dtype, output_dtype=output_dtype)
+    expected_q, expected_k = _reference(values)
+    actual = mla_q_cache_aiter_hip.run(**values)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert actual is values["out"]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual.float(), expected_q.float(), atol=0.02, rtol=0.02)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        values["kv_cache"][:tokens].float(),
+        expected_k.float(),
+        atol=0.02,
+        rtol=0.02,
+    )
+

+    torch.testing.assert_close(values["out"][:2], expected_q[:2])

+def test_fused_mla_q_cache_graph_replay_uses_changed_inputs():

+def test_writer_graph_survives_a_larger_eager_batch(writer):

+class TestKimiK3MlaQCacheWriterGate(CustomTestCase):
+    """The K3 writer replaces the split chain only where attention never reads its k,
+    and the cache holds the bytes the split chain would have written."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.writer = KimiK3RocmMlaQCacheWriter(kv_lora_rank=512, qk_rope_head_dim=64)
+        self.fused_q = torch.zeros(2, 12, 576, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        # The kernels are the boundary; the gate in front of them is under test.
+        self.writer._write_aiter = lambda **_: self.fused_q
+
+    def _write(self, *, attention_backend, is_target_verify, k_scale_float=1.0):
+        return self.writer.write(
+            q_nope=torch.zeros(2, 12, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            q_pe=torch.zeros(2, 12, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            k_nope=torch.zeros(2, 1, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            k_pe=torch.zeros(2, 1, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            out_cache_loc=torch.arange(2, dtype=torch.int64),
+            kv_cache=torch.zeros(4, 1, 576, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            k_scale_float=k_scale_float,
+            attention_backend=attention_backend,
+            is_target_verify=is_target_verify,
+        )
+
+    def test_triton_target_verify_keeps_the_split_chain(self):
+        """Triton target-verify runs the extend kernel, which reads k;
+        fusing it would feed that kernel the uninitialized k placeholder."""
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            self._write(attention_backend="triton", is_target_verify=True)
+        )
+
+    def test_fused_routes(self):
+        for backend, verify in (("aiter", False), ("aiter", True), ("triton", False)):
+            with self.subTest(backend=backend, verify=verify):
+                fused = self._write(attention_backend=backend, is_target_verify=verify)
+                self.assertIs(fused[0], self.fused_q)
+                self.assertEqual(tuple(fused[1].shape), (2, 1, 576))
+
+    def test_non_unit_kv_scale_keeps_the_split_chain(self):
+        """The split chain's AITER cache write casts without the KV scale,
+        while the fused kernels divide by it; their bytes differ unless it is 1."""
+        for k_scale_float in (None, 1.0):
+            with self.subTest(k_scale_float=k_scale_float):
+                self.assertIsNotNone(
+                    self._write(
+                        attention_backend="aiter",
+                        is_target_verify=False,
+                        k_scale_float=k_scale_float,
+                    )
+                )
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            self._write(
+                attention_backend="aiter", is_target_verify=False, k_scale_float=2.0
+            )
+        )
+
+    def test_missing_triton_fallback_keeps_the_split_chain(self):
+        """Off gfx950, an AITER build without the no-RoPE Triton kernel must fall
+        back to the split chain instead of failing the decode step."""
+        self.writer._write_aiter = lambda **_: None
+        with mock.patch.object(kimi_k3_rocm_mla, "_triton_q_cache_op", lambda: None):
+            self.assertIsNone(
+                self._write(attention_backend="aiter", is_target_verify=False)
+            )
+
+    def test_other_backends_keep_the_split_chain(self):
+        for verify in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(verify=verify):
+                self.assertIsNone(
+                    self._write(attention_backend="dsa", is_target_verify=verify)
+                )
+
+
+class TestMlaQCacheWriterCallSite(CustomTestCase):
+    """forward_absorb_rocm_core consults the writer only for non-DCP decode
+    and target-verify; every other step keeps the split chain."""
+
+    def _call(self, *, mode, dcp_enabled=False):
+        writer = mock.Mock()
+        attn = SimpleNamespace(
+            rocm_mla_q_cache_writer=writer,
+            attn_mqa=SimpleNamespace(layer_id=0, k_scale_float=1.0),
+            current_attention_backend="aiter",
+        )
+        forward_batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            forward_mode=SimpleNamespace(
+                is_decode=lambda: mode == "decode",
+                is_target_verify=lambda: mode == "target_verify",
+            ),
+            out_cache_loc=torch.arange(2),
+        )
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(
+                forward_mla_rocm,
+                "get_parallel",
+                return_value=SimpleNamespace(dcp_enabled=dcp_enabled),
+            ),
+            mock.patch.object(forward_mla_rocm, "get_kv_layers"),
+        ):
+            result = forward_mla_rocm.DeepseekMLARocmForwardMixin._maybe_fused_q_cache(
+                attn,
+                q_nope_out=None,
+                q_pe=None,
+                k_nope=None,
+                k_pe=None,
+                forward_batch=forward_batch,
+            )
+        return result, writer.write
+
+    def test_decode_and_target_verify_use_the_writer(self):
+        for mode in ("decode", "target_verify"):
+            with self.subTest(mode=mode):
+                result, write = self._call(mode=mode)
+                write.assert_called_once()
+                self.assertIs(result, write.return_value)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    write.call_args.kwargs["is_target_verify"], mode == "target_verify"
+                )
+
+    def test_dcp_and_extend_keep_the_split_chain(self):
+        """DCP decode all-gathers q from the split chain, and extend is not covered."""
+        for mode, dcp_enabled in (("decode", True), ("extend", False)):
+            with self.subTest(mode=mode, dcp_enabled=dcp_enabled):
+                result, write = self._call(mode=mode, dcp_enabled=dcp_enabled)
+                self.assertIsNone(result)
+                write.assert_not_called()
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `afa9dc5`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43127/checks?check_run_id=126468363717)

@yuychang The NV base `base-a-test-cpu` shard fails on this PR's own test, `test/registered/unit/models/test_rocm_mla_absorb_fusion_gate.py` ([job log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40808276640/job/123260121488)). Rerunning won't fix it:

```
ERROR: test_fused_routes (TestKimiK3MlaQCacheWriterGate) (backend='aiter', verify=False)
  File ".../kimi_k3_rocm_mla.py", line 120, in write
  File ".../kimi_k3_rocm_mla.py", line 45, in get
  File ".../torch/cuda/graphs.py", line 92, in is_current_stream_capturing
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
```

`_ZeroPositions.get()` calls `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` even when the device is CPU. The test is registered with `register_cpu_ci`, and the CPU runner has no usable CUDA driver, so the call fails there. One possible fix is to check the device type first:

```diff
-            if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            if device.type == "cuda" and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
```

(ROCm tensors also report `device.type == "cuda"`, so the graph-capture guard still applies on MI35x.) I haven't run the CPU test locally with this change, so please double-check that nothing else in the CPU path touches CUDA.
